newsitem.title: UK: RJB, Nat Power mulling new power station.
newsitem.headline: RJB, Nat Power mulling new power station.

text.p: British coal miner RJB Mining Plc said on Monday that it has teamed up with National Power Plc and Texaco Inc to assess the possibility of building a "clean coal" power station.
RJB has joined up with electricity generator National Power and U.S. oil company Texaco for a project that might build a 400 megawatt station in West Yorkshire, Northern England.
National Power said in a joint statement that the plant would cost about 300 million stg to build and that work could start next year and would take two years to complete.
National Power added that if the project was successfully developed in the UK, it has suitable sites for the development of further "clean" coal plants in the medium to longer term.
Keith Henry, National Power's chief executive said, "As the country's largest coal user, we are anxious to investigate all options to secure the future for coal."
